_doc:
A judgement asks what the change warrants on its merits; the comment compares the verdict with what the PR includes. Read by hack/pr-triage/pr_triage_llm.py.
Judgement keys: id, title, question, help_url (the title links there).
Evidence (what the PR includes): evidence_files (globs; a changed file counts unless removed) minus evidence_exclude (matching both: hidden from the model, not counted), or evidence_title / evidence_text (regex on the title / title and description). Evidence files are hidden from the model. skip_when_included: not asked when the evidence is present. surplus_ok: evidence the model deems unwarranted is not a mismatch. applies_to (globs): only asked and shown when a visible changed file matches.
Choice questions: choices (allowed verdicts); evidence_value {files, pattern}: the values the PR provides (group 1, added lines); absent_choice: the choice meaning nothing is warranted.
Flag questions have no evidence: a true verdict is the finding.
Top level: project {description, context, maintainers} (system prompt and comment text); model_defaults; max_diff_chars; show_first (globs shown first, so truncation hits the rest); exclude_patches (listed by name only); min_confidence (below it a mismatch is a weak signal); stale_after_commits (rebase notice); summary_from {files, pattern} (the author's own summary, given to every judgement).

project.description: You review pull requests for the Apache Solr Operator, a Kubernetes operator written in Go that manages Apache Solr clusters, together with its Helm charts and documentation.
project.context: Project layout: api/v1beta1 holds the CRD types (SolrCloud, SolrPrometheusExporter, SolrBackup) with their kubebuilder markers and field doc comments, which become the CRD schema. controllers/ holds the reconcilers and controllers/util the code that turns a CRD into StatefulSets, Services, Ingresses, ConfigMaps, PodDisruptionBudgets and init containers; controllers/*_test.go are envtest unit tests and tests/e2e are Ginkgo end-to-end tests on a KinD cluster. helm/solr-operator is the Helm chart that installs the operator; its Chart.yaml carries the release changelog under the artifacthub.io/changes annotation, and its README.md has a hand-maintained table of chart values. helm/solr is a convenience chart that creates a SolrCloud from values; it has the same Chart.yaml changelog and README table, and new SolrCloud spec options are normally exposed there too. docs/modules is the Antora documentation (solr-cloud/pages/solr-cloud-crd.adoc and siblings document CRD options; upgrade-notes/pages/upgrade-notes.adoc has per-version upgrade warnings). example/ has sample resources, hack/ build and release scripts, config/ the kustomize manifests. CRDs (config/crd, helm/solr-operator/crds), RBAC (config/rbac, copied into the chart), zz_generated.deepcopy.go and dependency_licenses.csv are generated by `make prepare` and their freshness is checked by CI, so never flag stale generated files. The oldest supported Solr version is 8.11 and the oldest Kubernetes version is 1.22; operator upgrades must not change a running SolrCloud unless the upgrade notes say so.

judgements.title: Operator chart changelog
judgements.question: Which changelog kind fits this change? The release changelog lives in helm/solr-operator/Chart.yaml under artifacthub.io/changes, and an entry is expected for every change a user of the operator would notice, including changes to controller code, init containers or the CRDs, not only to the Helm chart itself. added: a new opt-in capability, such as a new CRD field, a new helm value, or a new feature a user must enable. changed: an improvement or behaviour change that is not opt-in, such as a changed default, a changed generated pod spec, new RBAC permissions the operator needs, or a notable dependency upgrade (Go, Kubernetes libraries, controller-runtime, the Zookeeper Operator). fixed: fixes buggy behaviour with a user-visible symptom, such as a crash, a wrong manifest, a failing init container or a stalled reconcile. deprecated: marks a CRD field or helm value deprecated ahead of removal. removed: removes something previously deprecated. security: fixes a vulnerability or upgrades a dependency for a CVE. Answer (not-worthy) when no entry is warranted: pure refactoring, test-only changes, CI, build and release tooling, developer documentation, internal cleanup, typo fixes, and documentation-only changes.

judgements.title: Solr chart changelog
judgements.question: The PR changes the `solr` Helm chart (helm/solr), which has its own changelog in helm/solr/Chart.yaml under artifacthub.io/changes. Which changelog kind fits the change to that chart? added: a new chart value or template capability. changed: changed behaviour or defaults of existing values. fixed: a template or value bug with a user-visible symptom. deprecated and removed: as the words say. security: a vulnerability fix. Answer (not-worthy) when the chart change is only a comment, formatting or a version bump done by release tooling.

judgements.title: Chart README values table
judgements.question: Does this PR add, rename, remove or change the meaning, type or default of a Helm chart value in helm/solr-operator or helm/solr, such that the hand-maintained 'Chart Values' table in that chart's README.md should be updated? A new value always counts, including one only referenced from a template. Purely internal template changes that add no value and change no documented behaviour do not count.

judgements.title: User documentation
judgements.question: Does this PR add, change or remove something documented, or that ought to be documented, in the user documentation under docs/modules, such as a CRD field or its behaviour, a backup repository option, TLS or authentication behaviour, scaling or update behaviour, an operator command line flag, or a user-facing default? Helm chart values are documented in the chart README instead and do not count here; neither do internal changes, tests, CI or developer tooling.

judgements.title: Upgrade notes
judgements.question: Is this a change users must know about when upgrading the operator, warranting an entry in the upgrade notes? That includes: a removed or renamed CRD field or helm value; a changed default that alters the behaviour of existing SolrClouds; a change to the generated pod spec of existing SolrClouds (containers, init containers, volumes, env vars, probes, labels, annotations) that makes their pods restart when the operator is upgraded; new RBAC permissions the operator needs (users who manage RBAC themselves must add them); a raised minimum Solr, Kubernetes or Zookeeper Operator version; or a change to how existing resources (PVCs, Services, Ingresses) are handled. Purely additive, opt-in changes and bug fixes that do not change any existing resource do not warrant one.

judgements.title: Tests
judgements.question: Does this PR change non-trivial Go logic in api/, controllers/ or main.go (beyond refactoring, renames, logging, comments or kubebuilder markers) such that it should come with new or changed tests? Judge the code change itself: whether the diff already includes tests, or the description says tests were run, is irrelevant to whether tests are warranted. Controller changes are normally covered by the envtest unit tests in controllers/*_test.go, and behaviour that needs a running Solr by the Ginkgo e2e tests in tests/e2e. Helm templates, init container shell scripts, documentation, CI workflows and shell scripts under hack/ have no test harness here: the verdict is false for changes only to those. The exception under hack/ is the Python PR triage script hack/pr-triage/pr_triage_llm.py, which has unittest tests (hack/pr-triage/test_*.py): a logic change to it warrants a test too.

judgements.title: CRD option completeness
judgements.question: The PR changes the CRD types in api/v1beta1. Is a new or changed option incomplete? Look for: a field that is declared in the types but never read by the controllers to affect a generated resource (declared but not wired through); a field missing a doc comment or the usual kubebuilder markers (+optional, default or enum validation) that comparable fields have; a new field lacking a pointer or omitempty where the controllers need to tell 'unset' from 'zero'; or a new SolrCloud spec option that the `solr` Helm chart (helm/solr/values.yaml and templates, which you can see) ought to expose too but does not. Answer true only when something concrete is missing, and name it; answer false for complete options and for changes that only touch comments or markers.

judgements.title: Version compatibility
judgements.question: Does this change depend on behaviour that is not available across the whole supported range: a Solr CLI command, flag, API, system property, env var or Docker image layout that differs between Solr 8.11 and the latest 9.x (the `solr zk` CLI flags, `bin/solr` options, the prometheus exporter location, SOLR_TOOL_OPTS, health endpoints and security.json handling are known examples), or a Kubernetes API field, resource version or feature gate newer than Kubernetes 1.22? Also answer true when the change hardcodes a Solr version or image tag outside tests and examples. Answer false when the change is version-neutral or already guards on the Solr or Kubernetes version.

judgements.title: Testing notes
judgements.question: Is this a change whose correctness can only be shown against a running cluster, such as a Helm template change, an init container or shell script change, a change to how the operator calls Solr or ZooKeeper, or TLS, authentication, ingress or backup handling, and the PR description does not say how it was tested (which Solr version, Kubernetes flavour, scenario, or that e2e tests were run)? Answer false when the description does describe the testing, when the change is fully covered by unit tests, or when it is a documentation, CI or tooling change.
